summary: Olivia Chow is re-elected Toronto mayor, Carney says he is open to moving beyond the Indian Act, trade talks pick up, and the Bank of Canada decides on rates Wednesday.
body: Olivia Chow won a second term as Toronto's mayor on Monday. With 1,405 of 1,431 polls reporting, she had 54.1% of the vote to 41.1% for former councillor Brad Bradford, a wider margin than late polls suggested [^1]. She promised to keep property tax rises near inflation and to build more supportive housing and shelters [^1]. Elsewhere in the GTA, Alvin Tedjo was projected to win in Mississauga, and in Toronto Mike Layton won back the University-Rosedale council seat [^2].

At the first meeting of the prime minister, premiers and First Nations leaders in about two decades, Carney said he is committed to a process that "moves Canada beyond the Indian Act," the 1876 law that governs status, reserve lands and band councils, which could mean reforming or abolishing it [^3]. Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew had called for abolition. Carney said the federal government would not impose the change, and AFN National Chief Cindy Woodhouse Nepinak said First Nations must decide for themselves; there is no start date yet [^3]. Tensions remain over the law that speeds up approvals for major projects, which some First Nations leaders say could infringe their rights [^3].

On trade, Carney said talks with Washington had seen a "slight, slight intensification" and that any progress came because "the U.S. is coming closer to our position"; asked if Trump would honour a deal, he said "I don't know that" [^4]. On Wednesday, Oct. 28, the Bank of Canada is widely expected to raise its rate from 2.25% to 2.50%, with September inflation at 3.1%; markets price in about an 80% chance [^5]. Carney hosts EU leaders in Montréal on Thursday and Friday [^4].
differences: On the Indian Act, Carney says some participants, not all, raised abolition, and that First Nations will lead [^3]. On trade, Carney says the US is moving toward Canada, while White House adviser Kevin Hassett suggests a deal is close [^4].
